notes: The page assumes a) and b) for the geometric-fibre morphism, introduces a fibrewise algebraically trivial cycle and its class u(z), and claims containment in an i-star cohomology image modulo torsion after replacing S by a nonempty open.

The proof invokes statement 2), a curve and a correspondence over a finite extension K of k(s), a trace argument, a spreading-out assertion, a decomposition z=i*(z')+z'', and a null cohomology map; it then invokes statement 1) for vanishing of u(z''). These cited statements are not present in the permitted page packet and were not proved or independently checked.
The authorial reservation is exactly the live replacement “restriction probablement inutile, mais cet énoncé nous suffira pour ce qu'on veut en faire”; sans doute is cancelled.

Section 4 begins with Soient X un schéma projectif et lisse de dimension m and the pen insertion sur k Alg. clos, introduces a Lefschetz pencil, a blown-up variety and a morphism to P^1_k, then an open base and the final restriction map.
Diagnostic only: the top morphism visibly has X_sbar to X_sbar although later cycles and target cohomology involve Y. Both X capitals were retained without a domain correction.

Structural diagnostic actually performed: D1 has three opening parentheses after u(z) and only two closings; T8 has four opening parentheses in i*(H(...g(...))) but only three closings after n. Neither expression was repaired.
Diagnostic only: the two product capitals could not be settled as X versus Y from their overprints. No use was made of expected correspondence domains to override the ink.
No theorem proof, independent re-proof, numerical calculation, formal certificate, web lookup, OCR, compilation, or consultation of another page/reader was performed. check_events is therefore empty.

A fine vertical trace above b in fibres was inspected once. Its linguistic/authorial status remains uncertain; it is recorded in inventory and a TeX comment without inventing an extra source letter or drawing.

H's global conventions for a machine chi-shaped ell, underlined constant sheaves and emph-as-authorial-emphasis were credited. Missing handwriting wrappers alone were not counted as H errors. H's explanatory expectations were not treated as source text.
brief_feedback: The workflow was sufficient. One small clarification would help: specify how to encode an isolated ink-like trace whose authorial status is uncertain and that touches an otherwise legible letter (here above b in fibres), without inventing a character or introducing a block figure into an ordinary word. I recorded it in the inventory and an in-place TeX comment.
